newsitem.title: USA: BPA uncertain of need to purchase power in June.
newsitem.headline: BPA uncertain of need to purchase power in June.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) is still assessing whether it will need to purchase spot power to cover peak needs next month, sources at the Portland, Ore.-based federal agency said Thursday.
"We've got some (generating) capacity back and the weather is back to normal, but we are still deciding what to do for June," a BPA trader said.
A spate of hot weather in the Pacific Northwest earlier this month led BPA to purchase block power from other utilities, but those deals will expire at the end of May.
"We really saw some cooling load--that never used to happen in the Northwest," the trader said.
But industry sources note that new home developments and offices in the region now have central air conditioning as standard equipment.

BPA supplies were also squeezed earlier in May by flood control cutbacks at headwater hydropower projects such as Libby, with a capacity of 525 megawatts (MW), Hungry Horse (428 MW), and Dworshak (400 MW).
But the threat of flooding downstream of those project has faded for the time being, and they are back in operation, a BPA trader said.

BPA has also asked utilities to bring back on-line thermal units previously displaced with forward sales of hydropower, but some of that power is being turned back depending on real-time needs, the agency said.
